About The Opportunity

This is an open position with FirstEnergy Service Co., a subsidiary of FirstEnergy Corp.

The position reports to the Supervisor, Transmission Reliability in the AMRC Asset Management Support team. The successful candidate will be responsible for leveraging advanced statistical modeling to support reliability improvement initiatives. This includes but is not limited to predicting equipment failure impacts, weather impacts and predicting future reliability based on asset health, system maintenance and capital investment. The candidate will have strong communication and consultation skills to understand business needs across the organization. Develop tools and processes that provide visibility to key stakeholders and support improvement in FE transmission reliability.
Working across Power Delivery and Operational Excellence to ensure effective and consistent reporting and analysis.
Supporting NERC, NATF and other industry working groups associated with transmission reliability data recording, analysis, and reporting.
Conducting business specific research and ad hoc data analysis – obtaining data, interpreting results, and communicating findings to provide insights that reduce reliability risk, optimize investments, and improve transmission reliability.
Delivering quality and accurate work within established deadlines.
Providing storm support, as needed, including off-hours, weekends, and holidays.
Travel may be required at times across the FirstEnergy system.

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering or related field with minimum 4 years of relevant work experience.
Demonstrated proficiency in processing, manipulating, and generating insight from large data sets of structured and unstructured data.
Experience in the implementation of complex programs and projects.
Knowledge of statistical methods, predictive modeling techniques, and data mining algorithms is highly valuable.
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, R, or SQL.
Knowledge of FE systems: iTOA, OPPM, GIS, Cascade, EMS, SAP, and PI are preferred.
Ability to develop effective working relationships with employees at all levels of FirstEnergy to aid and resolve problems.
Excellent interpersonal skills, strong written and verbal communication skills, and strong analytical ability are required. Ability to effectively present complex subject matter to all levels of management.
Successful candidate must be a team player and possess a willingness to work in a team environment with an ability to work cross functionally.

jobs.description:
About Mantis

We help organizations improve how their buildings perform by bringing together energy, facility operations, and sustainability into one connected approach. At Mantis, our teams work across the full lifecycle of a facility—from planning and design to field execution and long-term asset management—across commercial and industrial portfolios, data centers, and complex mechanical systems.

Our work spans four core areas: Building Controls, Energy Efficiency, Energy Advisory, and Facility Management—covering HVAC/mechanical optimization, BMS/BAS and EPMS controls, lighting system upgrades, energy brokerage, roofing and building envelope assessments, construction management, and more.

Whether you’re in sales, engineering, construction/project management, field operations, corporate, or technology, you’ll play a role in delivering these solutions and helping clients improve facility performance.

Summary

The Survey Technician performs field inspections and data collection to assess the condition of building assets. This role gathers accurate field data, identifies facility defects and safety issues, and supports project teams with clear documentation and recommendations. Most of our survey work focuses on commercial roofing systems with opportunity to work on other facility assets including building envelope, pavement, lighting, HVAC, and more. This work schedule requires regular overnight travel for stretches of approximately 3 weeks at a time, which may increase or decrease depending on project requirements.

This role operates at the front lines of Mantis’ facility asset management methodology, with heavy use of our field-based Mantis Perform mobile app. Technicians serve as the face of the company on-site and play a critical role in capturing the data that drives client decisions. Work is completed in the field on client sites across the country under the direction of a Project Manager or Field Team Leader.

OUTCOMES (SCORECARD FOR SUCCESS)

Deliver complete and accurate survey data across assigned projects
Capture clear photos, measurements, and asset details using company tools
Identify and communicate asset conditions, defects, and safety concerns
Follow safety procedures and proactively address hazards in the field
Stay responsive and coordinated with project managers and team members
Keep data, time entry, and expenses up to date

Responsibilities

Perform field inspections across client sites to assess condition of building assets, systems, and surrounding areas
Use company-issued tablets and field tools to capture survey data, including measurements, GPS points, inventory, and condition details
Document defects clearly, including location, severity, and type of issue, using notes, photos, and system inputs
Take high-quality, complete photos of assets, defects, and site conditions to support reporting and analysis
Identify materials, components, and visible deficiencies during inspections and record findings accurately
Perform hands-on inspection activities such as measuring sections, navigating surfaces, and accessing different areas of a facility
Remove debris, clean drains or surfaces, and prepare areas to allow for accurate inspection
Perform minor field fixes during inspections (securing loose components, sealing gaps, basic patching) when appropriate

Identify and report safety hazards, site risks, or unsafe conditions; stop work when necessary
Follow all safety protocols, wear required PPE, and participate in job hazard analysis and safety briefings
Upload field data, photos, and notes on a regular basis and ensure all required documentation is complete
Communicate daily with project managers or field leaders on progress, issues, and site conditions
Complete administrative tasks including time tracking, expense reports, and responding to messages
Maintain a professional, customer-facing presence while working at client sites
Support other technicians and teams to complete project work

Minimum Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent
2+ years of commercial roofing, construction, or related field experience
Ability to use field data collection tools (tablet or mobile devices)
Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office

Preferred Qualifications

Experience performing roof inspections or roof repairs on steep slope roofs greater than 4:12 pitch
OSHA 10/30 and other safety certifications
IIBEC Certification: Registered Roof Observer (RRO)
AS/BS in Engineering, Construction Management, or related field
Roofing Technology Certificate

Working Conditions/Physical Requirements

Work schedule involves regular overnight travel for stretches of ~3 weeks at a time.
Ability to travel up to 80-90% (via vehicle, airplane, etc.)
Heavy physical demands, lifting up to 75 lbs. daily, standing up to 10-12 hours daily
Work is typically performed at height on low slope roofs (4:12 pitch) while utilizing proper fall protection and fall prevention equipment.
Work may be performed at height on steep slope roofs (greater than 4:12 pitch) while utilizing proper fall protection and fall prevention equipment.
Work is typically performed out-of-doors with exposure to all types of weather
Work is performed on or in the buildings of customers
Work requires safely climbing ladders daily
Work is performed in a non-smoking environment
Oral and auditory capacity enabling interpersonal communication as well as communication through automated devices such as email and phone
Working extended hours may be required as needed

Job Description

A Day in the Life:

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of data discovery and applied AI—where insights don’t stop at a slide deck, they go live. As an AI Solutions Engineer on our AI & Innovation team, you’ll hunt for patterns, anomalies, and untapped opportunity across Hertz’s operational and customer data, often surfacing answers that no dashboard has shown before. You’ll partner directly with business leaders and senior technical stakeholders to connect siloed data, challenge assumptions, and build capabilities that change how teams work with AI.

One week you may uncover an insight that reshapes a pricing decision; the next, you ship an AI agent or automated workflow that runs in production on a schedule. You’ll work in Databricks with Python and SQL, use AI-assisted development tools to move fast, and own the full path from notebook to live tool—pipelines, agents, lightweight apps, and knowledge systems included. You’ll also prove the value of what you build by establishing baselines, tracking outcomes, and showing leadership the real operational and financial impact of Hertz’s AI and automation investments.

Hunt across enterprise data—operations, customer behavior, pricing, and internal systems—for trends, anomalies, and opportunities that standard reporting never surfaces
Uncover hidden value where useful data sits in silos, incomplete or unconnected, waiting to change how a team operates
Curate and join multi-source datasets into analysis-ready assets on Databricks and similar platforms
Deliver analyses that move decisions, not just dashboards—with clear documentation of assumptions, lineage, and limitations

Build applied AI capabilities—agents, automated workflows, lightweight web apps, knowledge tools—that put data at the point of need
Utilizes Databricks, Python, SQL, and AI-assisted development tools to prototype fast and deliver production-quality solutions
Own the full journey from discovery to deployment, including refreshes, monitoring, and tight feedback loops with the teams using what you build
Quantify impact by establishing baselines, tracking outcomes before and after launch, and showing the real business value of AI and automation
Collaborates with business partners, senior technical leaders, and engineering teams across Hertz to validate findings and scale what works

As a Project Coordinator – Grant Engineering & Construction, at Stimulus Technologies, you’ll support the planning and execution of large-scale fiber builds by tracking engineering deliverables, permitting progress, and construction activity across multiple partners. You’ll work directly with project and construction leadership to ensure designs are delivered, permits are moving, and contractors stay aligned with the overall project schedule, especially on grant-funded projects where timing and documentation are critical.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys managing complex workflows and keeping multiple stakeholders aligned. You’ll track milestones across design, permitting, and construction, follow up with engineering firms and contractors on key deliverables, and help ensure everything is documented and audit ready. If you’re organized, proactive, and interested in the behind-the-scenes coordination that keeps large infrastructure projects moving, this is a strong opportunity to build experience in engineering and construction project delivery.

Essential Functions

Schedule and Deliverable Tracking

Maintain and update the master project schedule for Grant-funded projects under the direction of the Project Manager, tracking design, permitting, construction, and turnover milestones.
Track engineering firm deliverables including HLD, MLD, construction-ready design packages, permitting submittals, and as-built documentation against agreed-upon schedules.
Track construction contractor progress including mainline build, splicing, testing, and closeout activities against the project schedule.
Flag overdue or at-risk deliverables and milestone dates to the Project Manager and Construction Manager proactively.
Maintain project dashboards showing schedule performance, deliverable status, and construction completion percentages for internal leadership and client reporting.
Track and log all change orders, scope modifications, and schedule revisions with supporting documentation.

Engineering Firm and Contractor Coordination

Coordinate information flow between the Project Manager, Construction Manager, Permitting Manager, engineering firm, and construction contractors.
Follow up with the engineering firm on outstanding design deliverables, permitting submittals, inspection reports, and as-built packages.
Follow up with construction contractors on daily production logs, pay application documentation, and closeout deliverables.

new_jobs.description:
Coordinate the build. Track the moving pieces. Keep the project on course.

As a Project Coordinator – Grant Engineering & Construction, at Stimulus Technologies, you’ll support the planning and execution of large-scale fiber builds by tracking engineering deliverables, permitting progress, and construction activity across multiple partners. You’ll work directly with project and construction leadership to ensure designs are delivered, permits are moving, and contractors stay aligned with the overall project schedule, especially on grant-funded projects where timing and documentation are critical.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys managing complex workflows and keeping multiple stakeholders aligned. You’ll track milestones across design, permitting, and construction, follow up with engineering firms and contractors on key deliverables, and help ensure everything is documented and audit ready. If you’re organized, proactive, and interested in the behind-the-scenes coordination that keeps large infrastructure projects moving, this is a strong opportunity to build experience in engineering and construction project delivery.

Essential Functions

Schedule and Deliverable Tracking

Maintain and update the master project schedule for Grant-funded projects under the direction of the Project Manager, tracking design, permitting, construction, and turnover milestones.
Track engineering firm deliverables including HLD, MLD, construction-ready design packages, permitting submittals, and as-built documentation against agreed-upon schedules.
Track construction contractor progress including mainline build, splicing, testing, and closeout activities against the project schedule.
Flag overdue or at-risk deliverables and milestone dates to the Project Manager and Construction Manager proactively.
Maintain project dashboards showing schedule performance, deliverable status, and construction completion percentages for internal leadership and client reporting.
Track and log all change orders, scope modifications, and schedule revisions with supporting documentation.

Engineering Firm and Contractor Coordination

Coordinate information flow between the Project Manager, Construction Manager, Permitting Manager, engineering firm, and construction contractors.
Follow up with the engineering firm on outstanding design deliverables, permitting submittals, inspection reports, and as-built packages.
Follow up with construction contractors on daily production logs, pay application documentation, and closeout deliverables.
Route submittals, RFIs, design review comments, and approval requests to the appropriate parties and track response timelines.
Schedule and coordinate project meetings including weekly construction calls, design review sessions, and client status meetings; prepare agendas and capture meeting minutes and action items.
Maintain a running action item log across all project stakeholders and follow up on open items to drive closure.

Budget and Invoice Management

Process and log invoices from the engineering firm, construction contractors, pole owners, and permitting agencies; verify amounts against contracts, SOWs, and approved change orders.
Route invoices through the approval workflow and track payment status.
Track project expenditures against budgets and assist the Project Manager with variance reporting and cost forecasting.
Ensure all expenditures are properly categorized and documented to support Grant reimbursement submissions.
Assist with preparing cost summaries and budget reports for internal leadership and client reporting.

Grant Compliance and Documentation

Maintain organized, auditable project records in accordance with Grant program requirements, including schedules, budgets, invoices, deliverable logs, change orders, and correspondence.
Assist the Project Manager with preparation and submission of Grant progress reports, milestone certifications, and compliance documentation on schedule.
Compile construction production data, engineering deliverable status, and supporting documentation for grant reimbursement requests.
Track Grant reporting deadlines and ensure all required submissions are prepared and reviewed before due dates.
Maintain familiarity with Grant program rules, reporting templates, and compliance requirements; flag potential compliance risks to the Project Manager.
Support audit preparation by ensuring project files are complete, organized, and readily accessible.

Construction Documentation Support

Collect and consolidate daily and weekly construction production reports from the Construction Manager and engineering firm.
Update construction progress trackers with current data on route miles, strand miles, splicing, testing, and make-ready completion.
Track permitting status in coordination with the Permitting Manager; update the project schedule when new approvals or rejections affect the construction sequence.
Maintain organized files for construction documentation including inspection reports, daily logs, material delivery records, and contractor correspondence.
Prepare construction progress summaries for the Project Manager highlighting trends, variances, and areas requiring attention.

Education and Experience

Required

High school diploma or GED; associate or bachelor’s degree preferred.
Minimum 2 years of experience in project coordination, administrative support, or operations support, preferably in telecom, broadband, construction, or engineering.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook.
Experience with project tracking tools or scheduling software (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent).
Excellent organizational skills with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple concurrent tracking streams and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for coordinating across internal teams, external partners, and clients.
Ability to work independently and proactively follow up on open items without constant direction.
Travel up to ten percent.

Preferred

Experience supporting project management in telecom, broadband, or utility construction environments.
Familiarity with OSP fiber optic construction terminology, project phases, and deliverables (HLD, MLD, as-builts, splicing, testing).
Experience with BEAD, RDOF, ReConnect, CAF, or other government-funded broadband deployment programs.
Experience with grant compliance documentation, reporting, and reimbursement processes.
Familiarity with invoice processing, budget tracking, and basic cost reporting.
CAPM certification or coursework toward PMP.

Alignment with Core Values

At Stimulus Technologies, our core values define how we work. The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

Driven to Grow – Continuously seeks to develop professionally, stays current with industry practices, and pushes to improve processes and outcomes.
See a Need – Fill a Need – Proactively identifies gaps, obstacles, or opportunities and takes action without waiting to be asked.
